title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #11

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is the key question of this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. What is the price of food?
   B. How should we respond to instructions?
   C. Who is the tallest pupil?
   D. How far is the market?

2. Why is neat handwriting important? (1 mark)
   A. It is only for teachers
   B. It helps the reader to understand the message
   C. It makes the pencil last longer
   D. It makes the book heavier

3. Which pencil grip is best? (1 mark)
   A. Hold it by the end with your teeth
   B. Press it very hard
   C. Hold it lightly between the thumb and first finger
   D. Grip it with a fist

4. Which is a good way to practise the shape of a letter? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Rub it out
   C. Trace it in the air with your finger
   D. Cover it

5. A verb is (1 mark)
   A. a word that names a person
   B. a joining word
   C. a word that describes a colour
   D. a word that shows an action

6. In English, what usually happens to the voice at the end of a question? (1 mark)
   A. It becomes a whisper
   B. It stays exactly the same always
   C. It falls to silence
   D. It rises

7. What is reader's theatre? (1 mark)
   A. Acting with costumes only
   B. A reading test
   C. Reading a script aloud with different parts
   D. A drawing lesson

8. Which sentence needs a verb to be complete: Always ______ your hands with soap? (1 mark)
   A. your
   B. wash
   C. hands
   D. soap

9. In grammar, a verb is a word that (1 mark)
   A. names a place
   B. shows an action
   C. names a person
   D. joins two sentences

10. What is a resource person? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of book
   B. A person with special knowledge who visits to teach
   C. A bag for books
   D. A pupil who is late

11. What does inferring meaning mean? (1 mark)
   A. Spelling backwards
   B. Copying words
   C. Ignoring the word
   D. Working out meaning from clues

12. Why do we put ideas in order? (1 mark)
   A. To make the story shorter
   B. To confuse the reader
   C. To use more words
   D. So the reader can follow them

13. Which sentence is a simile? (1 mark)
   A. She is a sun.
   B. She is bright.
   C. She is as bright as the sun.
   D. She is a shining star.

14. What does pronunciation mean? (1 mark)
   A. The length of a story
   B. The way we say the sounds of words
   C. The way we write words
   D. The meaning of a word

15. What is a skit? (1 mark)
   A. A long poem
   B. A short play
   C. A list
   D. A picture

16. What should you do with the events of a story you tell? (1 mark)
   A. Tell them in the order they happened
   B. Mix them up
   C. Never mention the end
   D. Skip the beginning

17. What is a customer? (1 mark)
   A. A person who sells only
   B. A kind of shop
   C. A person who buys
   D. A type of money

18. What is a service? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of coin
   B. A thing you can hold
   C. A market
   D. Work done for others

19. What are the two main parts of a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Subject and predicate
   B. Title and ending
   C. Noun and verb only
   D. Capital and full stop

20. Which is a wild animal? (1 mark)
   A. Zebra
   B. Dog
   C. Cow
   D. Hen

21. Which pair of words rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. hen and goat
   B. day and play
   C. water and food
   D. cow and shade

22. What is a refrain? (1 mark)
   A. A rhyme only
   B. The title
   C. A line that is repeated
   D. A page

23. Why are stories important in communities? (1 mark)
   A. They waste time
   B. They teach values and keep history
   C. They hide the truth
   D. They cause trouble

24. Why should a writer plan a story before writing? (1 mark)
   A. To organise the ideas
   B. To avoid a title
   C. To skip the ending
   D. To lose the ideas

25. Which feeling does Ouch! show? (1 mark)
   A. Pain
   B. Joy
   C. Sleepiness
   D. Disgust

26. Which interjection shows sudden understanding? (1 mark)
   A. Aha
   B. Oops
   C. Ouch
   D. Yuck

27. What is a singing game with interjections? (1 mark)
   A. A story
   B. A silent game
   C. A written test
   D. A song where short exclamations show joy or surprise

28. What is role play? (1 mark)
   A. Acting out a situation
   B. Reading silently
   C. Copying
   D. Drawing only

29. Which adjective describes shape? (1 mark)
   A. round
   B. red
   C. heavy
   D. loud

30. What should you do after filling a form? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Give it to anyone
   C. Check it and sign and date it
   D. Throw it away

31. Which is a common field on a form? (1 mark)
   A. The number of windows
   B. Type of soil
   C. Colour of the wall
   D. Name

32. What does format mean for a form? (1 mark)
   A. How old it is
   B. Who wrote it
   C. What it costs
   D. How it is arranged on the page

33. Which is a polite way to interrupt? (1 mark)
   A. Stop talking!
   B. You are wrong!
   C. Excuse me, may I say something?
   D. Be quiet!

34. Which is a rude phrase? (1 mark)
   A. Excuse me
   B. Please continue
   C. Shut up
   D. Pardon me

35. Which of these is an action verb? (1 mark)
   A. lead
   B. very
   C. the
   D. is

36. What does answer when they call mean in the model poem? (1 mark)
   A. A leader shouts
   B. A leader hides
   C. A leader sleeps
   D. A leader responds when people need them

37. Does every poem have to rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. No
   B. Only long poems
   C. Only short poems
   D. Yes, always

38. What should you add when a task is dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. A warning
   B. A colour
   C. A song
   D. A joke

39. What should the title of an instruction chart do? (1 mark)
   A. Hide the task
   B. Tell what the task is
   C. Be blank
   D. Give a joke

40. Why do leaders need to give clear instructions? (1 mark)
   A. So people know exactly what to do
   B. To waste time
   C. To confuse people
   D. To make noise

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. State three steps for reading your part in a dialogue. (3 marks)

42. Write a short paragraph of three sentences about today's weather. Use at least one comma in a list, two capital letters for names and three full stops. (5 marks)

43. Explain how the meaning of You are coming to school changes when it is a statement and when it is a question. (3 marks)

44. List the two verbs in the sentence: The teacher counted the votes and announced the winner. (2 marks)

45. Complete with a preposition: The cat sleeps ______ the bed. (2 marks)

46. Choose one proverb and explain its meaning. Then describe a real situation at school where it would apply. (5 marks)

47. Explain what to do when you get a small burn and why. (4 marks)

48. State two uses of a full stop and a capital letter in a sentence. (2 marks)

49. Make an instruction chart of five steps for keeping the class clean. Include a title and start each step with a verb. (5 marks)

50. Create a form with four fields to find out classmates' favourite games. Include a title and instructions. (4 marks)

51. Explain what a form is. (2 marks)

52. Write a short speech of four sentences about caring for a goat. Use at least two prepositions. (5 marks)

53. Name three ways to practise letter shapes before writing them. (3 marks)

54. Give two sequence words. (2 marks)

55. Write one simile and one metaphor about a teacher. (3 marks)

56. Describe your favourite leisure activity using the who, where, when and why frame. (3 marks)

57. Explain why pace matters when reading a poem. (3 marks)

58. Describe what a written dialogue shows. (2 marks)

59. Describe what an imaginative composition is. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — How should we respond to instructions?
   The lesson asks how we should respond to instructions in songs and games.

2. B — It helps the reader to understand the message
   A message is useful only if it can be read.

3. C — Hold it lightly between the thumb and first finger
   A light grip prevents tiredness.

4. C — Trace it in the air with your finger
   Tracing helps the hand remember the movement.

5. D — a word that shows an action
   Verbs show what is done.

6. D — It rises
   Many questions end with a rising voice.

7. C — Reading a script aloud with different parts
   Pupils read parts with expression.

8. B — wash
   Wash is the action word that completes the sentence.

9. B — shows an action
   Verbs show actions.

10. B — A person with special knowledge who visits to teach
   A nurse visiting a class is an example of a resource person.

11. D — Working out meaning from clues
   Inferring uses clues in the context.

12. D — So the reader can follow them
   Order makes writing clear.

13. C — She is as bright as the sun.
   It uses as to compare.

14. B — The way we say the sounds of words
   Pronunciation is how words are said.

15. B — A short play
   A skit is a short acted scene.

16. A — Tell them in the order they happened
   Order helps listeners follow.

17. C — A person who buys
   A customer buys goods or services.

18. D — Work done for others
   Cutting hair is a service.

19. A — Subject and predicate
   Every sentence has a subject and a predicate.

20. A — Zebra
   Zebras live freely on the plains.

21. B — day and play
   Day and play end in the same sound.

22. C — A line that is repeated
   A refrain is repeated in a poem or song.

23. B — They teach values and keep history
   Stories teach and entertain.

24. A — To organise the ideas
   A plan gives the story shape.

25. A — Pain
   People say ouch when hurt.

26. A — Aha
   Aha shows realising something.

27. D — A song where short exclamations show joy or surprise
   Interjections can be part of songs.

28. A — Acting out a situation
   Role play acts a scene.

29. A — round
   Round describes shape.

30. C — Check it and sign and date it
   Checking prevents mistakes.

31. D — Name
   Name is a common field.

32. D — How it is arranged on the page
   Format is the layout.

33. C — Excuse me, may I say something?
   It asks permission politely.

34. C — Shut up
   Shut up is disrespectful.

35. A — lead
   Lead shows action.

36. D — A leader responds when people need them
   It means to respond to people's needs.

37. A — No
   Some poems do not rhyme.

38. A — A warning
   Warnings keep people safe.

39. B — Tell what the task is
   The title names the task.

40. A — So people know exactly what to do
   Clear instructions get work done safely.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, underline your lines, practise them, watch the punctuation, wait for your cue.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct sentences, for example On Monday in Kisumu the sky was cloudy. It was cool, windy and dry. Amina wore a sweater.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence that is complete and correct, one for a comma in a list and one for correct capitals.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: As a statement the voice falls and it tells something. As a question the voice rises and it asks something.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of the two meanings and one mark for the voice movement.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: counted, announced
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb. Teacher, votes and winner are nouns.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: under (or on, if it sleeps on top)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a preposition and one for a sentence that makes sense.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any correct proverb with a sensible meaning and a matching situation, for example A stitch in time saves nine means fix small problems early, such as mending a small tear in a uniform before it grows.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the proverb, two marks for the meaning and two marks for a clear situation.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Put it under cool running water for several minutes to reduce pain, cover it with a clean cloth and tell an adult or go to a clinic.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for cool water, the reason, clean cover and telling an adult.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: A capital letter begins a sentence and a full stop ends it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct use.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: Title: How to keep our class clean. 1. Sweep the floor. 2. Wipe the desks. 3. Put waste in the bin. 4. Wash your hands. 5. Close the windows.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the title, one mark for each of four steps that begin with verbs and are in order.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Title: Favourite Games. Instructions: Write neatly. Fields: Name, Class, Favourite game, Date.
   Working / marking points: One mark for title, one for instructions, two for four fields.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: A form is a page with spaces where people write information in an organised way.
   Working / marking points: One mark for a page with spaces and one for collecting information.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four clear sentences with two prepositions, for example Give the goat water beside the food. Build a shed behind the house. Do not put a heavy load on it. Call the veterinary doctor if it is sick.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence and one mark for correct prepositions.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Trace in the air, trace on a card, model with clay or string, paint them.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: first, next, then, finally (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Simile: The teacher is as patient as a rock. Metaphor: The teacher is a walking dictionary.
   Working / marking points: One mark for a simile, one for a metaphor, one for clearly showing the difference.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any clear description that says the activity, where and when it is done, with whom and why you like it.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for activity, place or time, and reason.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: A pace that is too fast makes words unclear, and one that is too slow loses interest. A good pace helps listeners follow and feel the mood.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of three ideas.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people written to show what each speaker says.
   Working / marking points: One mark for conversation and one for showing speakers' words.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: A story that comes from the writer's imagination and is not a true report.
   Working / marking points: One mark for story and one for imagination.
